correctness.rationale: Four selected closed neighborhoods cover at most sixteen vertices. In a dominating five-set with a points and b lines, 9-b<=3a and 9-a<=3b force a,b=2,3 in either order. The two-vertex shore must cover six different unselected vertices opposite it. For two points this forces a single point class, leaving precisely the three lines through the omitted classmate; for two lines it forces one parallel class x-y=constant, leaving exactly the three points on the omitted line. The converses use each transversal meeting each class once, and each cross-class point pair meeting on exactly one line. Same-shore class partners have distance four (they share no neighbor and are linked via a vertex in another class). The center meets three selected neighbors; the remaining vertices each have one witness and the selected set is independent. The translations and class cycle preserve incidence, and the listed duality swaps shores and preserves incidence; thus the center assignment is equivariant for a vertex-transitive action. This establishes the one orbit and all count and coverage assertions.
residual_risks: The finite check addresses just this 18-vertex graph; there is no assertion about higher domination coefficients or other geometries.
